title: Bounded execution of a shaped loop
statement: Fix a program environment, resource limits, and execution depth. Let $S(j,s,\mu)$ be a state for a counter value $j$, shape parameter $s$, and memory $\mu$, and let $I(j,\mu)$ be an invariant. Suppose $I(0,\mu)$ holds, and for each $j<n$, each $s$, and each $\mu'$ satisfying $I(j,\mu')$, the body can execute from $S(j,s,\mu')$ with cost at most $b$ to a state of the form $S(j,s',\mu'')$ with $I(j+1,\mu'')$. Suppose $Q(S(n,s,\mu'))$ holds for every $s,\mu'$ satisfying $I(n,\mu')$. Also suppose the state obtained by setting local $i$ to zero in the initial local store $\ell$ and using memory $\mu$ equals $S(0,s_0,\mu)$; for every $j\le n$ and every $s,\mu'$ satisfying $I(j,\mu')$, the bound expression is safe in $S(j,s,\mu')$ and evaluates there to $n$; the value of local $i$ in each $S(j,s,\mu')$ is $j$; and setting local $i$ to $j+1$ in $S(j,s,\mu')$ gives $S(j+1,s,\mu')$. If $n\le\mathrm{word}$ and $n(\mathrm{cost}(h)+b+7)+\mathrm{cost}(h)+5\le T$, then the counted loop starting from the state with locals $\ell$ and memory $\mu$ can finish with cost at most $T$ in a state satisfying $Q$.
hypotheses_covered: Each iteration for $j<n$ preserves the invariant and returns a state of the specified shape, with cost at most $b$
Every state of the specified shape at $j=n$ satisfying the invariant satisfies $Q$
The initial state with local $i$ set to zero equals $S(0,s_0,\mu)$
For every $j\le n$ satisfying the invariant, the bound expression is safe and evaluates to $n$ in $S(j,s,\mu')$
